answer: In a staked agent economy, influence is bought with locked collateral, not counted by identity. Each agent locks a bond as hard as quartz to earn the nectar of fees; voting power scales with stake, so splitting into a swarm of hollow sybil shells gains nothing. To seize a tenth of the votes an attacker must lock a tenth of all stake, and detected fraud slashes it. The cost is real capital held at risk, so minting fake identities never pays off.
